sections.html:
Midvale is a compact valley city: the Jordan River marks its western edge and Interstate 15 cuts down the middle. Residents numbered 36,028 in 2020, against 27,964 ten years earlier, a 28.8 percent climb helped along by new housing built over the old smelter ground out west.

Homes carry a median value of $436,600, and median gross rent runs $1,597. Just 43.4% of households own, which means plenty of Midvale houses change hands as rentals. Your buyer may be taking on tenants, an unfinished lease term or a landlord license, so those details can weigh more on the deal than a worn roof.

sections.h2: Bingham Junction and the old slag site
sections.html:
Bingham Junction is 446 acres of reclaimed land on the west side, where five smelters worked lead and copper ore from 1871 to 1958. Federal cleanup listed it as the Midvale Slag Superfund site, and a Ready for Reuse Determination in 2008 cleared it for shops, offices and homes. A light rail station opened there in 2011, and a supermarket and a park followed.

Just south, Jordan Bluffs covers 351 acres of the same slag ground and is still early in redevelopment, with proposals reaching toward 3,500 homes.

  • West side owners should keep whatever cleanup or closing paperwork came with their purchase. A lender or buyer may ask for it.
  • For one particular parcel, the title company can report what its search turned up.
  • Townhomes and condos near the station were bought with a wide mix of loans, and that can influence the financing a neighboring buyer lines up.

sections.h2: Light rail, freeways and main streets
sections.html:
Two TRAX lines, I-15 and a quick hop to I-215 make Midvale an easy base for valley commuters. The average trip to work is 20.6 minutes, and mentioning how close the nearest platform is will help your listing or your pitch to a buyer.

  • Red Line: stops at Bingham Junction and runs to the University of Utah.
  • Blue Line: stops at Midvale Fort Union and Midvale Center.
  • 7800 South is the east-west spine, and Main Street (700 West) passes the historic downtown.
  • The I-15 and I-215 interchange is near 7200 South and State Street, where a ski bus also runs.

Shopping clusters at the Shops at Fort Union on the east side and along State Street. Canyons School District serves most addresses, but its lines get redrawn now and then. Ask the district about your exact house before you name a school in writing.

sections.h2: Earthquake exposure on an older house
sections.html:
The Wasatch Fault underlies the valley, and its Salt Lake City segment last broke roughly 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Geologists put the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake somewhere on the fault at 57 percent over 50 years. Lake Bonneville left soft sediments across much of the Wasatch Front, which raises liquefaction concerns, and the magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 rattled all of Midvale.

With an older house, expect an inspector to check chimneys, water heater straps and foundation cracks. You have three choices: fix them first, disclose them, or sell as-is and hand the question to the buyer. Weigh the repair bill against the time you have.

The city wants every Midvale landlord to hold a landlord business license. Those renew on a different clock from other licenses: they expire August 31 and are due no later than September 15, while most other business licenses expire December 31 and fall past due after January 15.

The city council resets fee amounts each year, and a business that moves to a new address inside Midvale gets new inspections. Before you list a rental, confirm yours is current. Then gather the lease, the rent roll and the license itself in one folder. A buyer who inherits your tenants will ask for all three.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and the residential exemption
sections.html:
Salt Lake County values and bills Midvale property, running one calendar for every city in the county. Value is fixed as of January 1.

Tax stepDate
Assessor certifies valuesMay 22
Valuation notices mailedJuly and August
Board of Equalization window45 days from the original mailing
Tax notices mailedBy November 1
Pay by this day to avoid a penaltyNovember 30
Taxes become delinquentDecember 1

A primary residence in Utah is taxed on 55 percent of market value after a 45 percent residential exemption. That exemption does not follow the house to a new owner. The buyer must file, and the application goes to the county Board of Equalization by September 15. If you sell mid-year, tell your buyer about that deadline so they do not lose the discount.

The county recorder's counter is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, and it opens Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. Clerks there cannot draft or notarize paperwork, and they stay out of title disputes. After imaging, your original deed travels back by mail within two to three weeks. Your closing agent normally files it, so a trip downtown is rarely on your list.

sections.h2: Preparing a tenant-occupied house for sale
sections.html:
Landlords have homework that owner-occupants skip. Pull together the signed lease, any addenda, the current rent roll and your landlord license. Then speak with the tenant before anyone else does. Someone who hears about a sale from you is much likelier to agree to a walk-through, and surprises usually become delays.

Should the lease outlast your target closing date, say so in your first conversation. We can often buy with the tenant staying put, which lets the lease set the pace instead of blocking the sale. An empty unit needs no deep cleanout if you are selling as-is.

sections.h2: What to have ready at closing
sections.html: Plan to show a photo ID, plus the deed or the trust or estate papers if the house reached you that way, and a payoff figure if a mortgage is still open. Heirs should ask the title company early who is allowed to sign. This year's property tax is typically divided between you and the buyer at the table, and the title company can explain the split.

A cash purchase still ends with a deed recorded at the county. What disappears is the buyer's lender, the appraisal and the haggling over a repair list. Here is the usual order.

  • Tell us about the house, including tenants and anything that needs work.
  • We inspect and put a price on the house as it stands.
  • If the price works, a title company schedules signing and files the deed.
  • We settle on a closing day together.

Tenants, postponed repairs and estate paperwork do not rule a house out. An offer commits you to nothing, so you can walk away.

faqs.q: What is the population of Midvale, Utah?
faqs.a: Midvale counted 36,028 residents in 2020, up 28.8 percent from 27,964 in 2010. The estimate near the top of this page is more recent.

faqs.q: When are Midvale property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty on current-year real property tax. Unpaid balances turn delinquent on December 1.

faqs.q: Is Midvale in Canyons School District?
faqs.a: Yes. Canyons is the main district, with four elementary schools, two middle schools and Hillcrest High School. Use the district's boundary lookup for a specific address.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Midvale?
faqs.a: Yes, the city requires a landlord business license. It expires August 31 and is due no later than September 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Midvale house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. With owner-occupancy at just 43.4 percent, many sellers here are landlords. Give the buyer the lease and rent roll early so the closing date fits the lease terms.
